Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The Kiwi players are out in the middle. Dion Myers and Brian Bennett to open for Zimbabwe. Matt Henry to bowl first.
…THE RUN CHASE…

Chasing 191, Zimbabwe will need a composed and clinical batting effort to notch their first win of the season. Can they pull off the chase, or will New Zealand extend their unbeaten run? Stay tuned — the second innings is coming up shortly.

Richard Ngarava is up for a chat. He says injuries are always tough and he had to adjust a bit, but as a cricketer, things happen. Adds that the wicket is on the slower side, the conditions have made them to mix up pace. Tells there is responsibility on him but he has support from the youngsters around.

Zimbabwe showed promise with the ball, but a string of loose deliveries in the middle overs let the pressure slip. However, they bounced back impressively at the death, claiming a flurry of wickets to restrict New Zealand to under 200. Richard Ngarava was the standout performer with four wickets, while Tinotenda Maposa provided solid support with two. Sikandar Raza and Dion Myers were economical, though Trevor Gwandu’s expensive spell gave the Kiwis some breathing room.

A solid all-round batting performance from the Black Caps saw them post an impressive 190/6 in their 20 overs. After choosing to bat first, New Zealand suffered an early blow with the dismissal of Tim Robinson, but Rachin Ravindra and Tim Seifert steadied the innings superbly. The duo put on a commanding 108-run stand for the second wicket, with Ravindra scoring a fluent 63 and Seifert anchoring the innings with a powerful 75. Though the Kiwis lost a few quick wickets towards the end, a composed late cameo from Michael Bracewell ensured they reached a formidable total.
A couple of runs to end the innings! Slower ball on the full, outside off. Michael Bracwell drags it toward the wide of long-on and settles for two runs. New Zealand finish with 190/6.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now. The teams and the umpires make their way out to the ground. Tim Robinson and Tim Seifert make their way to open the innings for New Zealand. It will be Richard Ngarava to start with the ball for Zimbabwe. Let's play...

Pitch Report - Ed Rainsford and Tino Mawoyo are at the pitchside. They share that the pitch appears quite dry with several visible cracks, and it’s likely to behave similarly to previous matches, though it may play a bit slower. Closes by adding that batting first might not be a bad option after all.

Mark Chapman is up for a chat. He says that there's so much cricket these days, and first of all, it's really good to be back in international cricket, and it was a long flight from the USA. Adds that they pride themselves on playing good cricket, and they have got a good, balanced side. Mentions that they have got a new coach and they are trying different combinations.  Closes by adding that they changed the bowling attack last game, and Foulkes and O'Rourke came back, and they did not miss a beat.

Sikandar Raza, the skipper of Zimbabwe, says that batting first has been challenging, and they have come under fire for that.  Adds that this game matters more than any other game, in his opinion, when they win, the culture change develops a lot smoothly. He hopes to get things right and win today. Closes by adding that Dion Myers comes in for Wessly Madhevere.

Mitchell Santner, the New Zealand skipper, wins the toss and opts to bat. He says that it’s a used wicket and wants to put runs on the board. Shares that it’s a new challenge to set a target, and the guys are unsure of what might be a good score. Adds that it is the third game on this wicket, and it might be on the slow side. Mentions that playing games leading up to the major events helps them to be in good standing. Closes by adding that they have four changes to the side.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Dion Myers (in for Wessly Madhevere), Clive Madande, Sikandar Raza, Ryan Burl, Tony Munyonga, Tashinga Musekiwa, Wellington Masakadza, Tinotenda Maposa, Richard Ngarava, Trevor Gwandu.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert, Tim Robinson (In for Devon Conway), Rachin Ravindra, Mark Chapman, Bevon Jacobs (in for Daryl Mitchell), Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner(C), Zakary Foulkes, Matt Henry (in for Adam Milne), Ish Sodhi (in for Jacob Duffy), Will O'Rourke.

New Zealand, meanwhile, have ticked most boxes. Tim Seifert and Devon Conway have been among the runs, with Tim Robinson and Bevon Jacobs making the most of their chances. The bowling unit, led by Matt Henry and Jacob Duffy, has been potent, while Mitchell Santner and Adam Milne have provided control through the middle overs. Santner’s men will look to maintain their unbeaten run and carry momentum into the final. So, can New Zealand continue their dominance, or will Zimbabwe find one last spark to give their fans something to cheer about? Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned!

The Zimbabwean batters have struggled, failing to cross the 150-run mark in each of their outings. While Brian Bennett, Sikandar Raza, and Ryan Burl have shown flashes of form, they’ve lacked consistent support. With the ball, Richard Ngarava and Tinotenda Maposa have been standout performers, but the team needs a collective lift to finish their campaign on a high. Zimbabwe are reeling from three straight defeats and will be hoping to bow out of the tournament with a spirited performance in front of their home crowd.

As the T20I Tri-Series in Zimbabwe 2025 reaches its final league stage, all eyes turn to the sixth and penultimate match of the tournament, featuring the hosts Zimbabwe taking on an in-form New Zealand at the Harare Sports Club. This match might be a dead rubber in terms of qualification for the final, but both teams will be eager to end their league stage on a high. New Zealand have been the dominant force in this tri-series, showcasing their all-round brilliance by winning all three of their matches so far. Their consistent performances have already secured them a spot in the final on Saturday, where they are scheduled to face South Africa. For the Blackcaps, this game will serve as a crucial final dress rehearsal to fine-tune their strategies and maintain winning momentum before the championship clash. On the other hand, it has been a forgettable series for the home team, Zimbabwe. They have endured a challenging run, losing all three of their matches against both South Africa and New Zealand. While their chances of reaching the final are now extinguished, they will be playing for pride and a much-needed victory in front of their home crowd. A win here would provide a significant morale boost and offer some positive takeaways from the series.
